children.translated_text: <s>Āryaśrīmahādevīvyākaraṇam</s> (The Noble Prophecy of <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>) [also known as <s>Dvādaśadaṇḍakanāmāṣṭaśatavimalīkaraṇā</s> (The Purification through the Hundred-and-Eight Names in Twelve Stanzas)]

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutamekasamaye bhagavān sukhāvatyāṃ viharati sma mahatā bodhisattvasaṃghena sārdhaṃ - tadyathā avalokiteśvareṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mahāsthāmaprāptena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkaṃbhinā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena kṣitigarbheṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena samantabhadreṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ākāśagarbheṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena vajrapāṇinā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvabhayahareṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena evaṃ sarvamaṅgaladhāriṇā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvapuṇyalakṣaṇadhāriṇā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena candrasūryatrailokyadhāriṇā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvatīrthamaṅgaladhāriṇā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena maṃjuśriyā ca kumārabhūtena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena evaṃpramukhairbodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ / (
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavān</s>) was dwelling in <s>Sukhāvatī</s> together with a great assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — namely, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Kṣitigarbha</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvabhayahara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvamaṅgaladhārin</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvapuṇyalakṣaṇadhārin</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Candrasūryatrailokyadhārin</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvatīrthamaṅgaladhārin</s>, and the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful — headed by these and other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>.

body.text: atha khalvāryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandyaikānte nyaṣīdat / śrīrapi mahādevī bhagavantamevopasaṃkrāntā / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śatasahasraṃ pradakṣīṇīkṛtya sarvāṃśca tān sukhāvatīnivāsino bodhisattvān mahāsattvān śirasābhivandyaikānte nyaṣīdat /
body.translated_text: Then the noble <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side. <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s> also approached the Blessed One. Having approached, she circumambulated the feet of the Blessed One a hundred thousand times, bowed her head to all those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> dwelling in <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, and sat down to one side.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānanekaśatasahasrapuṇyālaṃkṛtastathāgatakoṭiparivṛtaḥ sarvaśakrabrahmalokapālastutastavitaḥ śriyaṃ mahādevīṃ dṛṣṭā mahābrahmasvareṇāvalokiteśvaraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat / yaḥ kaścidavalokiteśvara rājā vā rājamātro vā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā vā brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviṭśūdrā vā śriyā mahādevyā aṣṭottaraṃ śataṃ vimalaprakhyaṃ nāma stotraṃ dhārayiṣyanti tasya rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya viṣaye teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvabhayetyupadravā praśamiṣyanti / sarvacoradhūrtamanuṣyāmanuṣyabhayaṃ na bhaviṣyati / sarvadhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgāravivṛddhirbhaviṣyati / tasya ca rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya gṛhe śrīrnivasiṣyati / atha te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā evaṃ vācamabhāṣanta / sādhu sādhu (

children.text: ) bhagavan subhāṣiteyaṃ vāk / ye śriyā mahādevyā nāmadheyāni dhārayiṣyanti teṣāmapīmā guṇānuśaṃsā bhaviṣyanti /
children.translated_text: O Blessed One, well-spoken is this word! For those who shall preserve the names of <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>, these same benefits and blessings shall arise."

body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, adorned with hundreds of thousands of merits, surrounded by <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, praised and extolled by all <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, and world-protectors, seeing <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>, spoke thus to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> in a great <s>Brahmā</s>-voice: "O <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, whoever — whether a king, a royal minister, a <s>bhikṣu</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, <s>upāsaka</s>, or <s>upāsikā</s>, whether a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, or <s>śūdra</s> — shall preserve this hymn of <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>, the hundred-and-eight names called 'radiant as the stainless,' for that king or <s>kṣatriya</s>, in his domain, all fears, calamities, and afflictions of those beings shall be pacified. There shall be no fear from thieves, rogues, humans, or non-humans. There shall be increase of all wealth, grain, treasuries, and granaries. And <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) shall dwell in the house of that king or <s>kṣatriya</s>." Then those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> spoke thus: "Excellent! Excellent!

body.text: athāryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat / kutra bhagavan śriyā mahādevyā kuśalamūlamavaropitam / bhagavānāha / gaṃgānadīvālukāsamānāṃ tathāgatānāmantikāt śriyā mahādevyā kuśalamūlamavaropitam / bhūtapūrvamavalokiteśvara atīte 'dhvani ratnasaṃbhavāyāṃ lokadhātau ratnakusumaguṇasāgaravaidūryakanakagirisuvarṇakāṃcanaprabhāsaśrīrnāma tathāgato loke udapādi / tasyāntike śriyā mahādevyā kuśalamūlamavaropitamanyeṣāṃ ca bahūnāṃ tathāgatānāmantike / imāni ca tathāgatanāmāni tasyāḥ śriyā mahādevyāḥ kuśalamūlavivṛddhisaṃpattikarāṇi / sadānubaddhānitāni śriyā mahādevyā yānīha samudḥritāni sarvapāpaharāṇi sarvakilviṣanāśanāni sarvakāryavimalīkaraṇāni dhanadhānyākarṣaṇavivṛddhikarāṇi dāridryaparicchedanakarāṇi sarvadevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragāvarjanākarṣaṇakarāṇi sarvetyupadravopasargopāyāsasarvakalikalahavigrahavivādapraśamanakarāṇi ṣaṭpāramitāniṣpādanakarāṇi / (
body.translated_text: Then the noble <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: "Where, O Blessed One, did <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s> plant her roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>)?" The Blessed One replied: "<s>Śrī Mahādevī</s> planted her roots of merit in the presence of <s>Tathāgatas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. O <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, formerly, in the past, in the world-system called <s>Ratnasaṃbhavā</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnakusumaguṇasāgaravaiḍūryakanakagirisuvarṇakāñcanaprabhāsaśrī</s> arose in the world. In his presence, <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s> planted roots of merit, and in the presence of many other <s>Tathāgatas</s> as well. And these names of <s>Tathāgatas</s> bring about the growth and fulfillment of the roots of merit of <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>. These names, which are always bound to <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s> and which are set forth here, are removers of all evil, destroyers of all sins, purifiers of all endeavors, attractors and increasers of wealth and grain, eliminators of poverty, attractors and summoners of all <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, pacifiers of all calamities, afflictions, distresses, quarrels, disputes, conflicts, and contentions, and accomplishers of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections).

body.text: namaḥ śrīghanāya tathāgatāya / namo ratnakusumaguṇasāgaravaiḍūryakanakagirisuvarṇakāṃcanaprabhāsaśriye tathāgatāya / namo gaṅgāsarvatīrthamukhamaṅgalaśriye tathāgatāya / namaścandanakusumatejonakṣatraprabhāsaśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ samantāvabhāsavijitasaṃgrāmaśriye tathāgatāya / namo guṇasamudrāvabhāsamaṇḍalaśriye tathāgatāya / namo dhārmavikurvaṇadhvajavegaśriye tathāgatāya / namo jyotiḥsaumyagandhāvabhāsaśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ sattvāśayaśamanaśarīraśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ praṇidhānasāgarāvabhāsaśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ suparikīrtitanāmadheyaśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ asaṃkhyeyavīryasusaṃprasthitaśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ aprameyasuvarṇottaprabhāsaśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ sarvasvarāṅgarutanirghoṣaśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ prajñāpradīpāsaṃkhyeyaprabhāketuśriye tathāgatāya / namo nārāyaṇavratasannāhasumeruśriye (

children.text: ) tathāgatāya / namo brahmaśriye tathāgatāya / namo maheśvaraśriye tathāgatāya / namaścandrasuryaśriye tathāgatāya / namo gambhīradharmaprabhārājaśriye tathāgatāya / namo gaganapradīpābhirāmaśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ sūryaprabhāketuśriye tathāgatāya / namo gandhapradīpaśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ sāgaragarbhasaṃbhavaśriye tathāgatāya / namo nirmitameghagarjanayaśaḥśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ sarvadharmaprabhāsavyūhaśriye tathāgatāya / namo drumarājavivardhitaśriye tathāgatāya / namo ratnārciḥparvataśriye tathāgatāya / namo jñānārciḥ sāgaraśriye tathāgatāya / namo mahāpraṇidhivegaśriye tathāgatāya / namo mahāmeghaśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ smṛtiketurājaśriye tathāgatāya / nama indraketudhvajarājaśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ sarvadhanadhānyākarṣaṇaśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ saumyākarṣaṇaśriye tathāgatāya / namo lakṣmyākarṣaṇaśriye tathāgatāya / imāni tathāgatanāmāni satkṛtya dhārayitavyāni vācayitavyāni evaṃ sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: (Mount Sumeru of the Armor of <s>Nārāyaṇa's</s> Vow)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Brahmaśrī</s> (Glory of <s>Brahmā</s>)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Maheśvaraśrī</s> (Glory of <s>Maheśvara</s>)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrasūryaśrī</s> (Glory of Moon and Sun)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Gambhīradharmaprabhārāja</s> (King of the Radiance of the Profound <s>Dharma</s>)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Gaganapradīpābhirāma</s> (Delighting Lamp of the Sky)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Sūryaprabhāketu</s> (Sun-Light-Banner)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gandhapradīpaśrī</s> (Glory of the Fragrance-Lamp)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Sāgaragarbhasaṃbhava</s> (Born from the Womb of the Ocean)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Nirmitameghagarjanayaśas</s> (Fame of the Manifested Thunder-Cloud)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Sarvadharmaprabhāsavyūha</s> (Array of the Radiance of All <s>Dharmas</s>)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Drumarājavivardhita</s> (Increased by the King of Trees)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Ratnārciḥparvata</s> (Mountain of Jewel-Flames)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Jñānārciḥsāgara</s> (Ocean of Wisdom-Flames)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Mahāpraṇidhivega</s> (Speed of the Great Vow)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Mahāmeghaśrī</s> (Glory of the Great Cloud)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Smṛtiketurāja</s> (King of Mindfulness-Banners)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Indraketudhvajarāja</s> (King of <s>Indra's</s> Banner-Flags)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Sarvadhanadhānyākarṣaṇa</s> (Attraction of All Wealth and Grain)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Saumyākarṣaṇa</s> (Gentle Attraction)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Lakṣmyākarṣaṇa</s> (Attraction of Fortune)! These names of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> should be honored, retained, and recited; thus that son or daughter of good family will produce abundant merit (<s>puṇya</s>).

body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śrīghana</s> (Glorious Density)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Ratnakusumagunasāgaravaiḍūryakanakagirisuvarṇakāñcanaprabhāsa</s> (Jewel-Flower-Virtue-Ocean-Lapis-Lazuli-Gold-Mountain-Golden-Brilliance)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Gaṅgāsarvatīrthamukhamaṅgala</s> (Auspiciousness of the Gaṅgā and All Sacred Fords)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Candanakusumatejonakṣatraprabhāsa</s> (Sandalwood-Flower-Radiance-Star-Brilliance)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Samantāvabhāsavijitasaṃgrāma</s> (Universally Illuminating, Victor in Battle)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Guṇasamudrāvabhāsamaṇḍala</s> (Circle of the Radiance of the Ocean of Virtues)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Dharmavikurvaṇadhvajavega</s> (Speed of the Banner of Dharma-Transformation)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Jyotiḥsaumyagandhāvabhāsa</s> (Light-Gentle-Fragrance-Radiance)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Sattvāśayaśamanaśarīra</s> (Body that Pacifies the Dispositions of Beings)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Praṇidhānasāgarāvabhāsa</s> (Radiance of the Ocean of Vows)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Suparikīrtitanāmadheya</s> (Well-Proclaimed Name)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Asaṃkhyeyavīryasusaṃprasthita</s> (Well-Set-Forth with Innumerable Vigor)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Aprameyasuvarṇottaprabhāsa</s> (Immeasurable Golden Supreme Brilliance)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Sarvasvarāṅgarutanirghoṣa</s> (Sound of All Vocal Tones and Limbs)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Prajñāpradīpāsaṃkhyeyaprabhāketu</s> (Innumerable Light-Banner of the Lamp of Wisdom)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> whose glory is <s>Nārāyaṇavratasannāhasumeru</s>

body.text: vyākṛtā ca śrīmahādevī tathāgataiḥ / bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ śrīmahādevī anāgate 'dhvani śrīmahāratnapratimaṇḍitāyāṃ lokadhātau tatra śrīmaṇiratnasambhavo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyak sambuddhaḥ / sā ca lokadhāturnānādivyaratnapratimaṇḍitā bhaviṣyati / (

children.text: ) tatra ca lokadhātau sa eva tathāgata ālokakaro bhaviṣyati / te ca bodhisattvāstatra buddhakṣetre svayaṃprabhā bhaviṣyantyaparimitāyuṣaśca / ākāśataśca buddhadharmasaṅghaśabdo niścariṣyati / ye ca bodhisattvāstatra buddhakṣetre upapatsyante sarve te padmakarkaṭikāsūpapatsyante / tatra katamaddādaśadaṇḍakaṃ nāmāṣṭaśataṃ vimalaprakhyaṃ stotram / śṛṇu abhayāvalokiteśvara śriyā mahādevyā nāmāni / tadyathā sarvatathāgatābhiṣiktāsarvadevatābhiṣiktā sarvatathāgatamātā sarvadevatāmātā sarvatathāgataśrīḥ sarvabodhisattvaśrīḥ sarvāryaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaśrīḥ brahmaviṣṇumaheśvaraśrīḥ mahāsthānagataśrīḥ sarvadevatābhimukhaśrīḥ sarvadevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaśrīḥ sarvavidyādharavajrapāṇivajradharaśrīḥ catuḥpañcalokapālaśrīḥ aṣṭagrahāṣṭāviṃśatinakṣatraśrīḥ om sāvitrī dhātrī mātā caturvedaśrīḥ lakṣmīḥ bhūtamātā jayā vijayā gaṅgā sarvatīrthā sarvamaṅgalyā vimalanirmalakaraśrīḥ sarvapāpahantrī nirmadakarā candraśrīḥ sūryaśrīḥ sarvagrahaśrīḥ siṃhavāhinī śatasahasrakoṭipadmavivarasaṃcchannā padmā padmasambhavā padmālayā padmadharā padmāvatī anekaratnāṃśumālā dhanadā śvetā mahāśvetā śvetabhujā sarvamaṅgaladhāriṇī sarvapuṇyopacitāṅgī dākṣāyaṇī śatasahasrabhujā śatasahasranayanā śatasahasraśirā (
children.translated_text: And in that world-realm, that very <s>Tathāgata</s> will be the light-maker. And those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in that buddha-field will be self-luminous and of immeasurable lifespan. From the sky, the sound of '<s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Saṃgha</s>' will resound. And all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who will be reborn in that buddha-field will be born in lotus-calyxes. Now, what is the hymn called the 'Twelve Staves' (<s>Dvādaśadaṇḍaka</s>), the eight hundred [verses] shining with purity? Listen, O <s>Abhayāvalokiteśvara</s>, to the names of <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>! They are as follows: She who is consecrated by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; She who is consecrated by all deities; Mother of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; Mother of all deities; <s>Śrī</s> (glory) of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; <s>Śrī</s> of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; <s>Śrī</s> of all noble <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; <s>Śrī</s> of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>; <s>Śrī</s> who has attained the great station; <s>Śrī</s> who faces all deities; <s>Śrī</s> of all <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>; <s>Śrī</s> of all <s>vidyādharas</s>, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, and <s>Vajradhara</s>; <s>Śrī</s> of the four and five world-protectors; <s>Śrī</s> of the eight planets and twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions); <s>Oṃ</s>, <s>Sāvitrī</s>, <s>Dhātrī</s>, Mother, <s>Śrī</s> of the four <s>Vedas</s>; <s>Lakṣmī</s>; Mother of beings; <s>Jayā</s> (Victory); <s>Vijayā</s> (Conquest); <s>Gaṅgā</s>; [<s>Śrī</s> of] all sacred fords; All-Auspicious; <s>Śrī</s> who makes [all] pure and stainless; Destroyer of all sins; Maker of purity; <s>Śrī</s> of the moon; <s>Śrī</s> of the sun; <s>Śrī</s> of all planets; She who rides a lion; She who is concealed within a hundred thousand <s>koṭī</s> lotus openings; <s>Padmā</s> (Lotus); Born from the lotus; Dwelling in the lotus; Bearing the lotus; <s>Padmāvatī</s>; She with garlands of rays from many jewels; Giver of wealth; <s>Śvetā</s> (White); <s>Mahāśvetā</s> (Great White); White-Armed; Bearer of all auspiciousness; She whose limbs are endowed with all merit; <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s>; She with a hundred thousand arms; She with a hundred thousand eyes; She with a hundred thousand heads;

children.translated_text: She who bears a crown of various and wonderful jewels; Beautiful-formed; Universal-formed; <s>Yaśā</s> (Fame); <s>Mahāyaśā</s> (Great Fame); Gentle; <s>Bahujīmūtā</s> (Many-Clouded); Pure-haired; Moon-radiant; Sun-radiant; Auspicious; Maker of auspiciousness; She who faces all beings; Noble <s>Kusumaśrī</s> (Flower-Glory); <s>Kusumeśvarā</s> (Flower-Sovereign); <s>Śrī</s> of all <s>Sumeru</s> mountain-kings; <s>Śrī</s> of all rivers and streams; <s>Śrī</s> of all oceans of water; <s>Śrī</s> who faces all sacred fords; <s>Śrī</s> of all herbs, grasses, forest trees, wealth, and grain; Giver of gold; Giver of food and drink; Radiant; Light-maker; Pure-limbed; She who commands all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; <s>Śrī</s> who is the face of all hosts of <s>devas</s>; <s>Śrī</s> of <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, and <s>Vāsava</s>; Giver; Enjoyer; Splendor; Splendid; Power; Prosperity; Growth; Exaltation; <s>Dharmaśrī</s> (Glory of the Law); She who has <s>Mādhava</s> as her refuge; Dwelling in flowers; Without envy; She who is the refuge of human endeavor; She whose entire body is pure; <s>Maṅgalahastā</s> (Auspicious-Handed); Destroyer of all misfortune; <s>Śrī</s> who attracts all merit; <s>Śrī</s> of the whole earth; <s>Śrī</s> of all kings; <s>Śrī</s> of all <s>vidyādhara</s> kings; <s>Śrī</s> of all <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>; Radiance; She who delights in joy and fortune; <s>Śrī</s> purified by all sages; All-<s>Śrī</s>; The eldest and supreme <s>Śrī</s> of existence; The supreme <s>Śrī</s> of all <s>kinnaras</s> and all suns; She who dwells in blameless places; Beautiful; Maker of happiness; Beloved of <s>Kubera</s>; <s>Śrī</s> of the King of <s>Dharma</s>. <s>Oṃ</s>! Look upon, deliver, and liberate me from all sufferings! Turn toward me all accumulations of merit! <s>Svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ</s>! Turn toward me all sacred fords beginning with the <s>Gaṅgā</s>! <s>Svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ</s>! To <s>Sāvitrī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the bearer of all auspiciousness,

devi śrīvaiśravaṇāya svāhā / suvarṇadhanadhānyākarṣaṇyai svāhā / sarvapuṇyākarṣaṇyai svāhā / śrīdevatākarṣaṇyai svāhā / sarvapāpanāśanyai svāhā / sarvālakṣmīpraśamanyai svāhā / sarvatathāgatābhiṣiktāyai svāhā / sarvadevatābhimukhaśriye svāhā / āyurbalavarṇakarāyai svāhā / sarvapavitramaṅgalahastāyai svāhā / siṃhavāhinyai svāhā / padmasaṃbhūtāyai svāhā / sarvakṛtyakākhordavināśanyai svāhā / imāni tānyabhayāvalokiteśvaraśriyā mahādevyā nāmāni sarvakilviṣanāśanāni sarvapāpavidhvaṃsanakarāṇi sarvapuṇyākarṣaṇakarāṇi sarvālakṣmīpraśamanakarāṇi sarvaśrīsaubhāgyākarṣaṇakarāṇi / yaḥ kaścidvārayiṣyati imāni tathāgatanāmāni kalyamutthāya śucinā sarvabuddhānāṃ puṣpadhūpaṃ dattvā śriyai mahādevyai candanadhūpaṃ dattvā vācayitavyāni sarvaśriyamadhigamiṣyati sarvasukhasaumanasyalābhī bhaviṣyati sarvadevatāśca rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ kariṣyanti sarvakāryasiddhistasya bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text:
) <s>svāhā</s>! To the one embodied as the four <s>Vedas</s>, <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), <s>grahas</s> (planets), and hosts of celestial beings, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Rudra</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Viśvamukha</s> (the All-faced One), <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ nigrigrini, O accomplisher of all tasks, sini sini, I invoke you!
O Goddess! To the glorious <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To her who attracts gold, wealth, and grain, <s>svāhā</s>! To her who attracts all merit, <s>svāhā</s>! To her who attracts the <s>Śrī</s>-goddess, <s>svāhā</s>! To her who destroys all sins, <s>svāhā</s>! To her who pacifies all misfortune (<s>alakṣmī</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! To her who is consecrated by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To her who is the <s>Śrī</s> (splendor) facing all deities, <s>svāhā</s>! To her who bestows long life, strength, and beauty, <s>svāhā</s>! To her whose hands hold all that is pure and auspicious, <s>svāhā</s>! To her who rides a lion, <s>svāhā</s>! To her who is born from the lotus, <s>svāhā</s>! To her who destroys all <s>kṛtya</s> (sorceries) and <s>khorda</s> (malefic spirits), <s>svāhā</s>! These are the names of the great goddess <s>Abhayāvalokiteśvaraśrī</s> — they destroy all sins, they eradicate all evil, they attract all merit, they pacify all misfortune, they attract all auspiciousness and good fortune. Whoever recites these names of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, rising early in the morning, in a state of purity, having offered flowers and incense to all <s>Buddhas</s>, and having offered sandalwood incense to <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>, shall attain all prosperity, shall become one who gains all happiness and joy of mind, and all deities shall provide protection, shelter, and guardianship — the accomplishment of all tasks shall be his.

body.translated_text: And <s>Śrīmahādevī</s> was given a prophecy (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>: 'You, <s>Śrīmahādevī</s>, in a future age, in the world-realm called <s>Śrīmahāratnapratimaṇḍitā</s> (Adorned with Glorious Great Jewels), there shall be a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>) named <s>Śrīmaṇiratnasambhava</s> (Born of the Glorious Jewel-Gem). And that world-realm shall be adorned with various divine jewels.

body.text: idamavocadbhagavānāttamanā abhayāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan //
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One, and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Abhayāvalokiteśvara</s> was delighted. And that entire assembly, together with the world of <s>devas</s>, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.
